<div class="site-hero" style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#0f3460,#1a1a2e,#0a0a14);padding:56px 40px 48px">
  <div class="hero-badge">Conclusion</div>
  <h1>What We <span>Found</span></h1>
  <p>After 12 research questions, 6 descriptive analyses, and 6 ML models — here is what the data revealed about movie success.</p>
</div>

<div class="section">

<!-- CORE ANSWER -->
<div class="q-section">
  <div class="section-label">Core Answer</div>
  <div class="section-title">Movie success is multidimensional</div>
  <p style="font-size:1.05rem;color:#374151;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:24px">After combining descriptive analysis with machine learning across 12 research questions, the answer is clear: <strong>no single feature explains movie success alone.</strong> Ratings, votes, and revenue behave differently and are shaped by different combinations of factors.</p>

  <div style="background:var(--navy);border-radius:var(--radius-lg);padding:36px;color:#fff;text-align:center">
    <h3 style="font-size:1.2rem;font-weight:700;color:var(--gold);margin-bottom:12px">The Central Research Question</h3>
    <p style="color:#9ca3af;line-height:1.8;max-width:650px;margin:0 auto 20px;font-size:0.95rem">"Which movie characteristics best explain and predict a movie's success in terms of audience evaluation and financial performance?"</p>
    <div class="pill-row">
      <span class="pill gold">Genre matters for revenue</span>
      <span class="pill gold">Budget predicts scale</span>
      <span class="pill gold">log_votes predicts rating</span>
      <span class="pill gold">Star power → visibility</span>
      <span class="pill gold">Ensembles win</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- METHODOLOGY -->
<div class="q-section">
  <div class="section-label">Methodology Summary</div>
  <div class="section-title">Our Data Science Workflow</div>
  <div class="grid-4" style="margin-top:20px">
    <div class="step-card"><div class="step-num">1</div><div class="step-title">Load &amp; Clean</div><div class="step-desc">Parsed votes (K/M), duration, money fields, genres, dates from raw text</div></div>
    <div class="step-card"><div class="step-num">2</div><div class="step-title">Describe</div><div class="step-desc">Grouped summaries, visualizations across countries, genres, runtime, revenue</div></div>
    <div class="step-card"><div class="step-num">3</div><div class="step-title">Model</div><div class="step-desc">Train/test splits, feature selection, Ridge, ExtraTrees, GradBoost, RF compared</div></div>
    <div class="step-card"><div class="step-num">4</div><div class="step-title">Evaluate</div><div class="step-desc">MAE, RMSE, R², ROC AUC, F1, confusion matrices, feature importance</div></div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- DESCRIPTIVE INSIGHTS -->
<div class="q-section">
  <div class="section-label">Part 1 — Descriptive Analysis</div>
  <div class="section-title">What Patterns Exist in the Data?</div>
  <div class="grid-2" style="margin-top:20px">
    <div class="insight-card ic-green"><div class="insight-title">🌍 Country Shapes Ratings</div><div class="insight-desc">Smaller, selective industries show higher averages. Larger ones (US) show greater variation — prestige films alongside mass-market productions.</div></div>
    <div class="insight-card ic-blue"><div class="insight-title">🎭 Genre: Ratings ≠ Votes</div><div class="insight-desc">Documentary/biopic genres earn high ratings with fewer votes. Action and franchise genres drive massive audience size regardless of rating quality.</div></div>
    <div class="insight-card ic-gold"><div class="insight-title">⏱️ Non-linear Runtime Effect</div><div class="insight-desc">90–140 min films cluster at the highest ratings. Very short or very long films are far more variable. Runtime is not a strong standalone predictor.</div></div>
    <div class="insight-card ic-dark"><div class="insight-title">💰 Budget → Revenue (Imperfectly)</div><div class="insight-desc">Pearson r=0.685. High-budget films: 65.3% profitable. Low-budget films: 39.2% profitable. But ROI can go either way — outliers dominate.</div></div>
    <div class="insight-card ic-green"><div class="insight-title">⭐ Star Power → Visibility</div><div class="insight-desc">Well-known personnel boost vote counts and reach. But median ratings are identical (6.30) for high-profile and low-profile groups — fame ≠ quality.</div></div>
    <div class="insight-card ic-blue"><div class="insight-title">🎬 Action Genres Dominate Revenue</div><div class="insight-desc">Action Epic ($363M avg), Superhero ($310M), Animation ($284M) lead worldwide gross. International markets are a major driver.</div></div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ML INSIGHTS -->
<div class="q-section">
  <div class="section-label">Part 2 — Machine Learning</div>
  <div class="section-title">What Can Be Predicted?</div>
  <div class="grid-3" style="margin:20px 0">
    <div class="metric"><div class="metric-n">0.365</div><div class="metric-l">R² — Rating (GB)</div></div>
    <div class="metric"><div class="metric-n">0.645</div><div class="metric-l">R² — Revenue (GB)</div></div>
    <div class="metric"><div class="metric-n">87.3%</div><div class="metric-l">ROC AUC — Rating Class. (RF)</div></div>
    <div class="metric"><div class="metric-n">70.0%</div><div class="metric-l">Accuracy — Success (RF)</div></div>
    <div class="metric"><div class="metric-n">0.606</div><div class="metric-l">R² — Vote Count (RF)</div></div>
    <div class="metric"><div class="metric-n">0.484</div><div class="metric-l">R² — Release Timing (DT)</div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="grid-2" style="margin-top:16px">
    <div class="insight-card ic-gold"><div class="insight-title">🔑 Key ML Improvement: Log-Transform</div><div class="insight-desc">Applying log-transform to revenue and vote targets significantly improved all models. Raw skewed targets caused models to over-fit to blockbuster extremes.</div></div>
    <div class="insight-card ic-green"><div class="insight-title">🌳 Ensembles Always Win</div><div class="insight-desc">Random Forest, Extra Trees, and Gradient Boosting consistently outperformed Ridge/Linear baselines by capturing nonlinear interactions between features.</div></div>
    <div class="insight-card ic-blue"><div class="insight-title">🎯 Feature Selection Matters</div><div class="insight-desc">Reducing feature space to top 8 predictors improved performance and interpretability. log_votes, budget, and movie_age dominate rating prediction.</div></div>
    <div class="insight-card ic-dark"><div class="insight-title">⚖️ Balanced Training for Q3</div><div class="insight-desc">Removing ambiguous middle ratings and balancing the training set produced a much stronger confusion matrix for the high-rating classifier.</div></div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- LIMITATIONS -->
<div class="q-section">
  <div class="section-label">Limitations</div>
  <div class="section-title">What the Data Cannot Tell Us</div>
  <div style="margin-top:16px">
    <div style="display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:12px;padding:14px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);font-size:14px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7"><span style="font-size:1.1rem;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:2px">📢</span><span>Marketing spend and distribution size are not in the dataset — these are major real-world drivers of both revenue and visibility.</span></div>
    <div style="display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:12px;padding:14px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);font-size:14px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7"><span style="font-size:1.1rem;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:2px">🌐</span><span>Social media attention, critic reviews, franchise history, and streaming availability are missing — all influence modern audience engagement.</span></div>
    <div style="display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:12px;padding:14px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);font-size:14px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7"><span style="font-size:1.1rem;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:2px">📊</span><span>Appearance frequency is only a proxy for fame. A person appearing in many small films is treated the same as a global celebrity.</span></div>
    <div style="display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:12px;padding:14px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);font-size:14px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7"><span style="font-size:1.1rem;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:2px">🕐</span><span>The dataset covers a wide time range. Market conditions, audience tastes, and streaming economics have shifted significantly over decades.</span></div>
    <div style="display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:12px;padding:14px 0;font-size:14px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7"><span style="font-size:1.1rem;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:2px">🔮</span><span>Models predict broad revenue levels better than exact values. Viral hits and catastrophic flops remain fundamentally unpredictable from metadata alone.</span></div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- FINAL NOTE -->
<div class="q-section">
  <div class="section-label">Final Reflection</div>
  <div class="section-title">Why This Project Matters</div>
  <p style="color:#374151;line-height:1.8;font-size:1rem;margin-bottom:14px">This project demonstrates that careful data preparation — parsing text fields, transforming skewed targets, selecting features — matters as much as model selection. Many movie attributes begin as messy text, and converting them into clean numeric features was essential for all results.</p>
  <p style="color:#374151;line-height:1.8;font-size:1rem">Future work could add marketing data, streaming numbers, social media sentiment, and critic review scores to further improve predictions. Models could also be separated by era (pre- vs post-streaming) or by market (domestic vs international) to capture changing industry dynamics.</p>
